fixes.explanation: False is right. Jesus says, "But if your eyes are bad, your whole body will be full of darkness." Not a patch of it. The whole body, the same "whole body" He used for the light in the verse before.
Yes, false. Jesus says, "…not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these." Solomon had more riches than any king on earth (1 Kings 10:23). A lily still beat his wardrobe.

That's exactly what Jesus says. Treasure on earth is where "…moth and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal." Think of a cookie jar on an open counter. Somebody sneaks in and the cookies are gone, and I promise it won't be a moth.

Good guess, but that isn't in the verse. Jesus says the one who tries will "…hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other." He's talking about where love and devotion land. Nothing in the verse says the person ends up working for neither.

Jesus never says that, friend. He isn't calling food and clothes a waste. He asks, "Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?" The point is that life is more than food, and the body is more than clothes.

Fasting came up in the part of the sermon just before this (Matthew 6:16-18), but that's not what He's doing here. Jesus asks, "Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?" He's not ranking fasting over eating. He's saying life is more than food, and the body is more than clothes.
Right. Jesus says the birds "…do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and yet your heavenly Father feeds them." The birds aren't doing the farm work. Your heavenly Father is the one feeding them.

Not this time, friend. Jesus says, "…not even Solomon in all his glory was adorned like one of these." Solomon had more riches than any king on earth (1 Kings 10:23), and he lost to a flower. Imagine the royal tailors hearing that.

I see why it tempts, friend, because "deserve" feels like the natural word. But it isn't what He says. Jesus says, "…your heavenly Father knows that you need them." It isn't about what you've earned. It's about what your Father knows you need.

That's it. Jesus says, "But seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness…" He's just said not to worry about food, drink and clothes, and that the Gentiles strive after them. Now He tells them what to seek first.
